text:
marta: Heads-up — seeing a reproducible perf regression on Mixtral and Qwen variants when head_dim is non-multiple-of-8. p99 went up ~25% on production routing.
samir: Can you share traces? sounds like FlashAttention might be falling back. :thinking:
marta: Here's a short profile from a customer trace and local reproduction (seq_len=1024, batch=8, head_dim=48).
```
# nvprof-like summary (sanitized)
Kernel: flash_attn_fwd       time: 1.8ms   calls: 640
Kernel: sdpa_fwd             time: 6.1ms   calls: 640  <-- big jump
Kernel: triton_matmul        time: 0.3ms   calls: 128
Memcpy H2D                 0.5ms
Total tokens/sec dropped ~22%
```
marta: The runtime logs show: "flash_attention: unsupported head_dim 48 -> falling back to SDPA" and then a fallback to a Triton matmul for masked KV handling.
jess: That log string is exactly what we saw in a perf regression last month with a Mistral model. Mask handling + head_dim odd -> SDPA path used which does extra masking copies.
kevin: Two angles: (1) kernel-level: flash/SDPA code expects padded head dims (multiple of 8 or 16); (2) runtime-level: batching heuristics sometimes group requests with mixed head dims and force slow path. Also KV cache shapes get reallocated when we pad, causing more memcpys.
samir: Repro script would help. If someone can produce a minimal run that toggles head_dim 48 vs 64 we can isolate where the cost is (kernel compute vs memcpy).
marta: I made a tiny harness: pad_head=true/false, use stepwise seq len growth, toggled prefix cache on/off. Quick snippet:
```
# pseudo
for head in [48,64]:
  model = load_model(head_dim=head)
  run_infer(batch=8, seq=1024, use_kv_cache=True)
  profile()
```
```
Observed:
- head=48: SDPA used, memcpy spikes at 0.4ms per step
- head=64: flash_attn used, lower latency
```
kevin: Important note: padding at runtime fixes kernel choice but increases per-token FLOPs ~+6-12% and increases GPU memory slightly. Not great for Dedicated customers on cost SLOs.
perf-bot: benchmark: mixtral-8k head48 vs head64, batch8, seq1024 -> p50: 16.2ms vs 14.1ms, p99: 48.8ms vs 36.9ms
jess: KV cache behavior: did you notice cache alignment changes? If padding toggles the kv stride, the runtime may allocate new KV tensors each request, killing caching benefits.
marta: Yes — when we pad at runtime we currently allocate a new buffer and copy KV into it; that explains memcpy spikes. Suggestion: instead of realloc, keep a padded buffer per model variant and memcpy only once on model load or on first request for that variant.
samir: Short-term mitigation: adjust kernel selection policy to prefer flash-compatible variants when available (even if slightly older model) and add a per-customer flag to force padded model artifacts. Long-term: update SDPA/Flash kernels to accept arbitrary head dims or implement efficient padded views without copies.
kevin: Also consider batching heuristic change: avoid mixing head-dim-odd requests in the same micro-batch. Group by compatible head_dim to avoid fallback for the whole batch.
jess: I'll file an infra ticket with repro instructions + attach perf traces. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml to decide if we want runtime padding or kernel work first.
marta: Blocking item for Dedicated SLOs — rolling forward without mitigation will hit customers with mixed-serving workloads. Can we do a canary change to do padding only for routes that specify higher SLOs?
samir: Agree. Plan:
- short (1 week): implement grouped batching by head_dim + runtime per-model padded cache (no per-request copies)
- medium (2-4 weeks): add runtime flag to prefer padded artifacts and validate cost impacts in canary
- long (quarter): upstream kernel work to remove head-dim constraints in Flash/SDPA or add an optimized Triton fallback that avoids extra copies
kevin: I'll prototype grouped batching today and add tracing hooks for memcpy counts.
jess: I'll create the ticket and add the perf-bot outputs + sample nvprof traces.
marta: Thx — please ping when the grouped batching change lands so I can run the canary on the problem customer. :rocket:
perf-bot: note: creating issue #RT-4123 (headdim-kernel-fallback) with attached perf logs
samir: tagging @kevin to follow through on tracing + @jess on the canary plan
kevin: on it. :thumbsup:
